_readme: agents/composer.py builds every email from this file. The AI never writes a sentence about you: it only picks up to two 'areas' from the list below and copies one short phrase describing the company from the company's own website — and code verifies both against the site text. Every sentence here comes from the CV. Edit freely, but any number you add must also be listed in verified_facts.allowed_numbers (a test enforces it). No tool names on purpose: the email talks about what you built, the CV lists the tools.

email.subject: {target_role} from February 2027 — {topic} | {applicant_name}
email.intro_with_hook: I'm a final-year Computer Engineering student at ENSIT in Tunis, specialised in cybersecurity and AI engineering. What interests me most about {company} is your work on {hook}.
intro_standard_variants: I'm a final-year Computer Engineering student at ENSIT in Tunis, specialised in cybersecurity and AI engineering, and I'm really interested in becoming part of the team at {company}.
I'm a final-year Computer Engineering student at ENSIT in Tunis, specialised in cybersecurity and AI engineering, and I'd genuinely like to join the team at {company}.
I'm a final-year Computer Engineering student at ENSIT in Tunis, specialised in cybersecurity and AI engineering, and joining the {company} team is something I'm really interested in.
email.match_lead_one: Your focus on {area_1} is where my own experience is strongest.
email.match_lead_two: Your focus on {area_1} and {area_2} maps directly onto my own experience.
email.motivation: My path into AI grew directly out of wanting to automate my own security methodologies.
email.internship_ask: I'm looking for an end-of-study internship starting February 2027, in the final year of my Bac+5 engineering degree, and I'm open to continuing with the team afterwards.
closing_variants: My CV is attached with more detail. I'd be glad to discuss how I could contribute to {company}, and I look forward to hearing from you.
My CV is attached with further detail. I'd be genuinely glad to bring this background to {company} and grow with the team — I look forward to hearing from you.

areas.label: offensive security
areas.match_description: Penetration testing, red teaming, vulnerability assessment or research, application security, bug bounty, attack surface management.
areas.evidence: I built RedBox, an autonomous AI red-teaming platform that finds vulnerabilities in live, deployed applications: it has solved 60+ CTF challenges automatically and reported 3 real vulnerabilities in production environments.
areas.alt_evidence: At Forvis Mazars, I built an LLM assistant that helps pentesters validate their findings and generate professional reports.

areas.label: AI-driven security
areas.match_description: A security company whose product or service is itself built on AI, machine learning or automation.
areas.evidence: At Forvis Mazars, I built a RAG-based LLM assistant for pentesters that validates its findings against public vulnerability and attack-technique data, with a deterministic check that reduces hallucinations in the reports it generates.

areas.label: security operations and threat detection
areas.match_description: SOC, SIEM, threat detection and response, MDR/XDR/EDR, security monitoring, incident response, blue team, threat intelligence, managed security.
areas.evidence: At TDS Global by Nomios, I helped build an AI-powered SOC, including network anomaly detection that reached 97% accuracy on the CICIDS dataset and a malware scanning and monitoring component.

areas.label: malware analysis and reverse engineering
areas.match_description: Malware analysis, reverse engineering, binary or firmware analysis, digital forensics, DFIR.
areas.evidence: Reverse engineering and digital forensics are the CTF categories I compete in, and the ones I design challenges for as President of Securinets ENSIT.

areas.label: agentic AI
areas.match_description: LLMs, generative AI, AI agents, multi-agent systems, RAG, copilots, autonomous agents.
areas.evidence: I design agentic systems end to end: my Carthage Connect platform coordinates 7 specialised AI agents with retrieval and document processing, and at Talan I worked on multi-agent orchestration for an applied-AI pipeline.

areas.label: machine learning
areas.match_description: Machine learning, data science, predictive modelling, anomaly detection, analytics.
areas.evidence: My machine learning work includes a network anomaly-detection model that reached 97% accuracy on the CICIDS dataset during my internship at TDS Global by Nomios.
areas.alt_evidence: I also hold NVIDIA's certificate in Applications of AI for Predictive Maintenance.

areas.label: cloud infrastructure
areas.match_description: Cloud platforms, cloud security, DevOps, DevSecOps, infrastructure, Kubernetes.
areas.evidence: I've deployed and operated production workloads on AWS, configured their security groups, and I'm currently completing the AWS Solutions Architect – Associate certification.

areas.label: software engineering
areas.match_description: General software, SaaS, web or mobile products, digital agencies, IT services with no explicit security or AI focus.
areas.evidence: I build complete products rather than prototypes: Carthage Connect, for example, is a 50+ page web application with 7 AI agents behind it.

strengths.text: My flagship project is RedBox, an autonomous AI red-teaming platform that has solved 60+ CTF challenges automatically and reported 3 real vulnerabilities in production environments.
I've completed three internships — at Forvis Mazars, Talan and TDS Global by Nomios — building AI systems for security teams and applied-AI projects.
I've won several national and international CTF competitions, and as President of Securinets ENSIT I organise competitions and mentor younger students.
